learningObjective: Contrast `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` with the default automatic-dynamic behavior and identify their trade-offs.

canonicalClaims.claim: `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` requests symbolic-shape tracing from the first compile; the default automatic behavior first specializes on observed shapes and only promotes a dim to dynamic after several distinct sizes are seen.
nonImplications: Does not imply `dynamic=True` is always faster than default; specialized kernels can be faster on hot shapes.
Does not imply that all dims become symbolic; some computations force specialization.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It changes what the tracer records; the graph is different.
Compilation still occurs; only shapes are treated symbolically.

misconceptions.claim: `dynamic=True` produces numerically different outputs due to lower precision.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Precision is not affected by the dynamic flag itself.

misconceptions.claim: The default never recompiles regardless of input shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Default may specialize on each new shape until auto-promotion kicks in.

implementationFacts: `dynamic=True` traces with SymInts from the first compile
`dynamic=False` forces static specialization for every new size
performanceScenarios: Choosing between static specialization and dynamic tracing is a trade-off between compile-cache size and per-shape kernel performance.
